articleTitle: Application of the TMS320E17 DSP in a low power speech scrambler
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: This paper describes a demonstration voice scrambling unit developed by the Centre for Communications Research at Bristol University, in conjunction with British Telecom. The scrambling technique and its practical implementation are outlined. Particular attention is given to the circuit implementation and techniques adopted to minimise power consumption.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analysis of algorithms for digital controller for brushless AC motor using a TMS320C25 microprocessor
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: Describes a novel Hardware/Software design and implementation for an entirely digital permanent magnet AC Brushless Control system based on a single Texas Instruments TMS 320 C25 microprocessor. The main objective of the work is to explore a purely digital implementation with a single microprocessor solution and the associated signal processing requirements for such an implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: The latest generation of DSPs has enabled a new range of algorithms to be implemented in real-time. An inevitable side-product of this is that algorithms developed for much slower processors will now run many times faster than real-time. This, along with a suitable on-chip serial interface, enables a single DSP to process several channels on a PCM stream in real-time. The principle behind DSP multi-tasking is that every task should process a frame of data, after which it releases control of the processor at least until its next frame is ready. The neatest and most flexible way of achieving this is with a nonpreemptive scheduling mechanism, with a device driver to handle the input and output of sampled data. This paper briefly describes the multi-tasking operating system, the approach taken to software development on the DSP32C, and some applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A secondary feature algorithm for pitch determination of speech signals and its implementation in real-time using a Motorola DSP56001 based system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: The pitch of speech is a useful parameter both in its own right and as a means of improving the estimates of other parameters. For instance, formant analysis is used to estimate the shape of the vocal tract and hence determine the speech sound uttered. If a reliable pitch estimate is available, then pitch-synchronous analysis may be used to estimate the formants, yielding a better result. Although reliable pitch estimates may be obtained using a transducer known as a laryngograph, it is generally a requirement of a practical system that the processing is carried out on the speech signal itself, i.e. the electrical signal obtained using a microphone. This paper presents an algorithm for pitch determination of speech, and discusses its implementation using digital signal processing technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: This paper presents implementations of adaptive signal processing applications on the noncanonical A100 FIR filter using controlling transputers. These applications when performed using the least mean squares (LMS) algorithm, generally use a canonical transversal filter with feedback of an updating error signal to iterate the filter weight vector according to the LMS algorithm which, in the mean, yields the Weiner-Hopf solution. This paper shows that it is not possible to implement LMS algorithm for the noncanonical FIR filter. Using both mathematical analysis and cut-set graph theoretic techniques it is shown that, although similar to the LMS, what is realised is a variant which is labelled the noncanonical LMS (NC-LMS). Inverse system modelling and beamforming using the NCLMS have been implemented on the transputer/A100 system and are presented in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital signal processors applied to Kalman filtering with radar tracking applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: The Kalman filter is suited to radar target tracking but places a high numerical workload on Radar Data Processors (RDP). Using a Motorola 56000 DSP as a Kalman filter coprocessor frees RDP time for other tasks. Computing power is increased and more sophisticated tracking algorithms than hitherto possible can be run in real time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience gained implementing a DSP teaching laboratory at BIHE
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: The Institute has been involved in teaching DSP since 1983. The original work was based on 6800/6809s, then the Intel 2920, but is now based on the TI TMS320 family. Currently the DSP facilities consist of six TMS32010 based workstations with TMS32030/25s available for 3rd year Honours/Degree projects and staff research/consultancy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A DSP teaching system using the Texas Instruments TMS320C25
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: Discrete-Time Systems and Digital Signal Processing (DSP) have been taught for more than five years at the University of Reading. In 1989/90 some practical work in DSP was introduced for second year BEng Honours students in Electronic Engineering. This paper describes a practical audio-band DSP system based on the Texas Instruments TMS320C25 processor, together with an outline of the practical work now being run with the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Small frequency shift of audio signals by digital signal processing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: One of the methods to reduce oscillation due to feedback in a Public Address system is to shift the frequency of input signal by a few hertz at the output. This paper describes how the small frequency shift is achieved by Digital Signal Processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: Automatic recognition of speech by machine for inferior to that of most humans. However there are applications such as 'hands-free' car telephone dialling, and aircraft cockpit instrument selection, where the benefits provided by current technology justify the use of real-time systems. This paper describes the implementation of a real-time recogniser, constructed as part of an ESPRIT II project entitled Adverse-Environment Recognition of Speech. Details are given of implementation issues, and solutions chosen.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: The Vector Signal Processor (VSP) is designed for use as a co-processor and has a bus structure and timing regime suitable for operation in a manner similar to microprocessor peripherals with a DMA interface. The architectural philosophy for the microword organisation has been approximately categorised as 'horizontal'. The main features of this structure are outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multi-digital signal processing architecture for fast Fourier transform implementation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Practical Applications of DSP Devices
abstract: A hybrid parallel and sequential architecture may be the optimum solution to the calculation of the FFT. The authors have constructed such a system consisting of three TMS 320C25 digital signal processors. Two of the processors work in parallel, performing 256-point radix-4 decimation in frequency 'in place' complex FFTs. The third processor combines the outputs of the other two processors thus forming the full 512-point FFT. It also performs the unscrambling of the data from the preceding processors and the digit reverse procedure prior to outputting the results. The system has been constructed on two IBM PC/AT plug-in cards with the interfacing to the IBM being carried out via its I/O ports.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
